diagnosis.root_cause: A migration deploy to users-service triggered heavy database locking (db_lock_wait_sessions spiking from ~1 to over 55) which caused signups and profile updates to fail with write errors and timeouts.
evidence: A migration deploy went out to users-service just before the incident started at ~20:11 UTC.
users-service write_error_rate spiked from 0.001 to 0.6089 starting at 20:14 UTC.
users-db db_lock_wait_sessions spiked from ~1 to over 55 starting at 20:12 UTC.
database-degradation.md runbook suggests killing or pausing the offending query/transaction or rolling back/adjusting the migration.
diagnosis.recommended_fix: Roll back the offending migration deploy on users-service or identify and kill the blocking transaction/query on users-db causing the lock wait sessions. Follow up by refactoring the migration to avoid locking active write tables during peak traffic.

evidence.plan_reasoning: Signups and profile updates are failing with timeouts after a migration deploy to users-service, so we should search the users-service logs for database or migration errors around the incident start time.

Since the specific migration log search returned nothing, we should check the error rate metrics for users-service and the database lock wait sessions for users-db to see where the bottleneck is occurring during signups and profile updates.

[1] database-degradation.md > Mitigation (score 0.3536)
Kill or pause the offending query, transaction, or batch job. Add the missing
index or pin the plan. Route reads away from lagging replicas. Raise connection
limits only as a stopgap. Schedule heavy maintenance away from peak.

[2] bad-deploy-correlated-regression.md > How to confirm (score 0.3477)
- Line up the incident start against deploy history for the affected service.
  A deploy whose timestamp precedes the first symptom by 1 to 10 minutes is a
  strong lead.
- Check whether hosts on the new build differ from hosts still on the old build.
- Look for errors that name a specific new rule, flag, or code path.

[3] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > Mitigation (score 0.3303)
Relieve the downstream slowdown or cut the offending traffic. Then isolate pools
per dependency, size them for peak concurrency, add acquisition timeouts, and fix
any code path that fails to release a connection.
